title: Cain and Abel
lead: Adam and Eve's sons. Cain murdered his brother Abel out of jealousy (Genesis 4), and became the Bible's first picture of the path of anger, envy and violence.

sections.b: God accepted Abel's offering but not Cain's. God warned Cain that "sin is crouching at the door," but Cain killed Abel in the field. Asked where his brother was, he answered, "Am I my brother's keeper?" He was sent away as a wanderer, with a mark to protect him from being killed (Genesis 4:1–16).

Jesus names Abel as the first martyr (Matthew 23:35). Hebrews 11:4 says Abel offered his sacrifice "by faith," and 12:24 contrasts his blood with Jesus's. 1 John 3:12 warns believers not to be like Cain: "he was from the evil one."
